Operator manual · Safety and moderation

Reports and takedowns

How members report posts, people and Pulse items, where the reports land, and what each action really does.

How members report

In the app, members report a post, a person or a Pulse item and choose a reason: spam or scam, offensive content, misleading post, or other. A note of up to 500 characters goes with it. Blocking someone in the phone app also files a report.

  • A member can file at most 10 reports an hour.
  • Reporting the same thing again, while the first report is still open, does nothing new.
  • Nobody can report themselves.

The report form tells members their note goes to moderators. In practice it goes to the owners and admins, because moderators cannot sign in to Settings.

Where reports land

People and Safety, then Triage and Moderation. Any owner or admin can act on them.

  • The list shows every report ever made, handled or not, and the count beside the tab counts them all. Work from the newest.
  • It does not show which post a report is about. Open the reported person to see their posts, or ask the reporter.

What each action does

  • Dismiss Flag: marks the report reviewed. Nothing happens to the person.
  • Freeze Accounts: freezes the person's credit line and their voting. It does not mark the report handled.
  • Remove from the Pulse (for Pulse items): hides the item from the Pulse and marks the report handled. The person is not suspended.
  • To stop a person using the community, Suspend them from their page (see Members and invites). Members then vote on keeping it.

Taking a post down

In Triage and Moderation, find the post in the posts list and delete it.

  • If someone had paid for it and the beans were still held, they get them back. Open requests are cancelled. An event is cancelled, and people going to it get a cancellation notice.
  • Settings calls this permanent, but the record stays in the database, hidden. It cannot be brought back from Settings.
  • The author is not told, and nor is the person who reported it. Send them a message yourself.

Prune Stale Posts removes every post older than the age you pick, including ones that are still live and wanted. Use it with care.

Be fair

  • Read the post and talk to the person before you act, unless there is danger.
  • Write reasons you would be happy for the whole community to read. Suspension reasons are public.
  • Whoever is reported may be a stranger to you, from a culture you do not know. Ask before you judge.
